benchmark_kind_note: Field-space trajectories are scored against SYNTHETIC deterministic ground-truth routes projected through real per-frame homographies. This is an engineering benchmark of the trajectory layer, not a measurement of NFL or broadcast tracking accuracy.
real_multiframe_trajectory_accuracy_note: Real multi-frame trajectory accuracy is not yet measured: no real broadcast clip with frame-level ground-truth trajectories is available in this project. Real frames are used for single-frame smoke/integration and geometry-refusal tests only.

gate_warmup_ablation.note: Computed by run_phase4_benchmark() from the shipped implementation, TRAIN/VAL only (TEST is not consulted, so warm-up selection cannot leak into the frozen split). The innovation-gate threshold is unchanged; the shipped rule delays the gate until a track has two accepted updates (M-of-N track initiation).

detector_metric_separation_note: Detection counts/precision/recall in this file are FIXTURE HARNESS pass-through statistics (the boxes are scheduled by the harness, not predicted from pixels). They must never be reported as player-image-detector accuracy; image-based detector accuracy is unmeasured.
acceleration_note: Acceleration is the finite difference of the smoothed filter velocity, bounded by a plausibility clip. It is EXPERIMENTAL AND NOT VALIDATED: no measured acceleration accuracy is claimed, and the reported error is dominated by the filter's own noise floor rather than by a validated acceleration model.
uncertainty_note: The reported covariance is an a priori engineering model (footpoint pixel noise propagated through the homography Jacobian plus a propagation-drift allowance). It is NOT statistically calibrated against data: empirical coverage is reported per split, per geometry state, and before/after the smoothing stage, and the gap is explained rather than tuned away. Do not read the reported sigma as a calibrated confidence interval.

uncertainty_calibration_analysis.coverage_note: A value of k2 > 1 means the empirical error is larger than the reported covariance (intervals too narrow). Fitting an inflation factor and shipping it would change the reported uncertainty and could change gate behaviour; that is a Phase-5 decision, so nothing was changed here.
uncertainty_calibration_analysis.counterfactual_note: TEST is evaluated with the TRAIN/VAL-fitted scale exactly once, for documentation. No threshold, constant, or reported value in this benchmark uses it.

inputs: sample lifetime (number of trajectory samples emitted for the track)
dominant_track_selection.tie_break: lowest track_id (deterministic; independent of dictionary/iteration order)
dominant_track_selection.gt_dependency: Ground truth is used ONLY to attribute a track to the player it is scored against (an oracle association inherent to every labelled MOT benchmark: an error cannot be computed without knowing which player a track is compared to). That association is computed before, and never influences, the selection itself.
dominant_track_selection.note: Selection is reproducible from runtime-observable counters alone. Fragmentation is additionally reported for every non-dominant track (see track_table / fragmentation_taxonomy), so a poor dominant track cannot hide fragment tracks.

fragmentation_definitions.legitimate_new_track: First track attributed to that ground-truth player in the sequence, and not created at an injected outlier event.
fragmentation_definitions.active_association_swap: A track for the player appears in a frame where the player's previous track is still present (both tracks exist in that frame at least momentarily: an active-association swap, the identity failure Phase 3 reports as 0).
fragmentation_definitions.post_expiration_reinitialization: A track for the player appears after the previous track for that player had no sample in the re-acquisition frame (expired / missed / dropped out): a post-expiration re-initialization rather than a swap.
fragmentation_definitions.outlier_induced_spawn: The track's first sample coincides with an injected outlier event for that player (the corrupted measurement was strong enough to spawn a separate track).
fragmentation_definitions.unmatched_spurious_track: A track that the harness cannot attribute to any ground-truth player. Expected to be 0 in this harness because every fixture detection carries a label; reported so that a non-zero value is visible rather than silently dropped.

rejection_accounting_definition.clean_sample: A dominant-track sample whose (player, frame) pair is NOT an injected outlier event, and for which a raw field projection exists (so the innovation gate could act on it).
rejection_accounting_definition.clean_sample_rejected: A clean sample that the innovation gate rejected: the false-rejection event.
rejection_accounting_definition.corrupted_sample: A dominant-track sample at an injected outlier event (the manifest injects a known pixel jump); 'accepted' means the corrupted measurement was folded into the track.
rejection_accounting_definition.innovation_gate: Field-space chi-square test on the Mahalanobis distance between the measurement and the constant-velocity prediction. This is the only gate that can REJECT a measurement.
rejection_accounting_definition.plausibility_gate: Image-space footpoint jump limit. It can only FLAG a sample (and only when geometry is unknown), never reject a measurement, so its count is reported separately and is not part of the false-rejection rate.
rejection_accounting_definition.note: 'Clean'/'corrupted' are harness labels from the manifest, not labels inferred from ground-truth error: this block is a harness metric, not a model-internal quantity.

note: harness_gt_dependent = requires ground-truth player coordinates to exist at all
harness_label_dependent = requires harness event labels (injected outliers, dropouts) or map-side GT association, not model internals
model_observable_no_ground_truth = computable from the emitted samples alone

benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.player_motion: Synthetic deterministic field-space routes (straight lines, tanh-blended cuts, speed ramps). Timings, speeds and jitter are engineering fixtures, NOT recorded NFL player trajectories.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.footpoints: Box fixtures generated by projecting the synthetic field-space ground truth through the real per-frame broadcast/All-22 homography of the base images, plus deterministic pixel jitter. FixturePlayerDetector (fixture_detector_v1) supplies the boxes.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.geometry: Per-frame CalibrationResult objects: real Phase-1 calibrations of the base frames for calibrated frames; explicit failure objects for unknown frames; T(drift) composed variants flagged is_temporally_propagated for propagated frames.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.image_detector_accuracy: UNMEASURED. Phase 4 measures the trajectory layer given projected player positions; it is not evidence that image-based player detection is solved.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.team_labels: TEAM_A / TEAM_B remain permutation-invariant appearance clusters; trajectory metrics do not depend on real-world team identity.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.camera_cut: Camera cuts are modelled as an abrupt synthetic framing change plus explicit calibration refusal objects (failure_reason='camera_cut_uncalibrated'). Real broadcast cuts also change scene content, exposure and motion blur, which are not modelled: this scenario validates the refusal/recovery state machine, not real cut detection accuracy.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.benchmark_kind: synthetic_trajectory_benchmark: field-space trajectories are scored against synthetic deterministic ground truth projected through real per-frame homographies of the base images. It is an engineering benchmark of the trajectory layer, not a measurement of NFL/broadcast tracking accuracy.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.real_multiframe_trajectory_accuracy: NOT MEASURED. No real broadcast clip with frame-level ground-truth trajectories exists in this project. Real frames are used only for a single-frame integration smoke test and for the Phase-2/3 geometry-refusal gates.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.uncertainty: NOT STATISTICALLY CALIBRATED. The reported covariance is an a priori engineering model (footpoint pixel noise through the homography Jacobian plus a propagation-drift allowance). Empirical coverage is published per split, per geometry state, and before/after the smoothing stage; the reported sigma must not be read as a calibrated confidence interval.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.acceleration: EXPERIMENTAL / NOT VALIDATED. Acceleration is the finite difference of the smoothed velocity with a plausibility clip; only mathematical correctness is unit-tested and no accuracy claim is made.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.ground_truth_usage: Ground truth exists only in the benchmark harness (fixture boxes and synthetic routes carry a gt_id through detector metadata). The production package (football_vision/) reads no ground-truth identifier; the trajectory layer's provenance passthrough is opt-in and empty by default. Dominant-track selection uses runtime-observable counters only, and TEST is never used to select a threshold, constant, warm-up rule, process-noise value, uncertainty model or track.

frozen_parameters.note: All constants were fixed a priori (documented engineering assumptions) before TEST was evaluated.

split_protocol.train: Used to confirm the a priori gate/process-noise assumptions produce stable kinematics.
split_protocol.val: Used to check jump-rejection behaviour and camera-motion handling.
split_protocol.test: Strictly held-out frozen split; zero thresholds or model constants tuned on TEST.

identity_contamination.note: Tracks whose samples carry more than one ground-truth label. Per-sample attribution (CLEAR convention) keeps the identity metrics honest; these rows exist so the contamination itself stays visible.

rejection_accounting.note: Split-level values are sums over sequences; the three median_* fields are medians of per-sequence medians (documented approximation, not a pooled median).

uncertainty_diagnostics.note: Split-level coverage/uncertainty values are medians of per-sequence values (documented approximation); jitter/model pixel sigmas are weighted by fixture footpoint count. Coverage is measured on CLEAN accepted measurements; the *_including_injected_events variants keep the pre-remediation view (corrupted-but-accepted samples included) visible.
uncertainty_diagnostics.footpoint_jitter_stats_note: observed_* and assumed_* pool the per-sequence values weighted by the number of fixture footpoints; see uncertainty_diagnostics per sequence for the full derivation.

determinism_check.note: wall-clock runtime fields excluded; one sequence from each split (TRAIN, VAL, frozen TEST) re-run through the identical code path

process_noise_ablation.note: Comparison of the only constant that could attenuate real motion (the filter's process-noise acceleration scale). Measured on TRAIN + VAL only; TEST is excluded so this cannot be used to tune the frozen split. Shipped value remains 5.0.

real_frame_smoke_test.note: Single-frame smoke test only: one still frame cannot exercise multi-frame trajectory, smoothing, camera motion, or occlusion behaviour.

limitations: Player motion is synthetic deterministic field-space ground truth projected through real per-frame homographies: an engineering fixture, not recorded NFL trajectories. Real multi-frame trajectory accuracy is NOT measured.
Detection boxes are fixture boxes (fixture_detector_v1); image-based player detection accuracy remains unmeasured and no detection-accuracy number in this file is a detector metric.

The reported covariance is an a priori engineering model and is NOT statistically calibrated; empirical coverage is reported per split and per geometry state, and the gap is explained (jitter vs assumed pixel noise) rather than tuned away.
Acceleration is experimental: it is a clipped finite difference of the smoothed velocity, not a validated acceleration estimator.

Fragmentation is split by a deterministic taxonomy (active association swap / post-expiration reinitialization / outlier-induced spawn / legitimate new track / unmatched). The taxonomy is exhaustive and asserted against the track count, but the categories are harness-visible states, not inferred internal tracker modes.
Camera pan/zoom is applied as an exact synthetic image-space transform; real broadcast camera motion also changes perspective, rolling shutter, and motion blur.
One single-frame real-frame smoke test (no ground truth) plus geometry-refusal/integration tests only: no real multi-frame broadcast clip was available in this phase.
